claimChecks.evidenceQuote: A procedure is a document you write in plain language.

claimChecks.claim: Auxx describes retrieving matching source passages and citing them in replies.
claimChecks.evidenceQuote: The AI fetches the top-matching snippets at answer-time and cites them inside the reply.

claimChecks.evidenceQuote: A procedure is a document you write in plain language.

scoreChecks.reason: A narrow prototype can use sample records and plain-language procedures; live inbox integrations add setup work.
scoreChecks.evidenceQuote: A procedure is a document you write in plain language.

scoreChecks.reason: A support team is a plausible buyer hypothesis given a described support burden; the source does not establish demand or revenue.
scoreChecks.evidenceQuote: He was drowning in support messages (dealing with returns, product questions, sales, etc) and didn’t have a good way to organize and attack them

scoreChecks.reason: One ticket type, a small sample inbox, retrieval, and draft review are a bounded student experiment; the full CRM is outside scope.
scoreChecks.evidenceQuote: A procedure is a document you write in plain language.

scoreChecks.reason: The described product can start from schedules or ticket events and draft/update records; people set procedures and review sensitive replies.
scoreChecks.evidenceQuote: Seven ways to start A schedule, a record change, an installed app, an inbound webhook, an @mention, a ticket assignment, or a direct message.

scoreChecks.reason: First-party page text includes workflow screens and a demo link, but does not independently verify use or outcomes.
scoreChecks.evidenceQuote: Start free trial Try demo app.auxx.ai/app/chats

completedAssessment.reason: The sole proposed support-inbox post has fresh first-party workflow evidence, bounded human review, a plausible but unvalidated buyer hypothesis, and independently checked scores at the frozen threshold.
